3D voxel model: one layer per standard depth level

Source: R/AllClasses.R, R/create_3d_objects.R, R/show-3d.R
SpatVoxel-class.Rd

A SpatVoxel is a terra::SpatRaster in which depth is the layer index and the cell values are the variable (temperature, oxygen, presence, ...). Each layer's depth is stored in terra's own per-layer field, terra::depth(), in metres positive down; depths must be set, distinct and ordered shallow to deep. Read them with depths(). as_voxel() names the layers {variable}_depth={value} when it sets the depths, as labels for people to read. The package never reads depths from layer names, so renaming the layers doesn't change their depths. The depth axis is grid-wide: every cell is sampled at the same set of standard depths.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'SpatVoxel'
c(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVoxel'
subset(x, subset, negate = FALSE, NSE = FALSE, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVoxel,numeric'
x[[i, j]] <- value

# S4 method for class 'SpatVoxel,character'
x[[i, j]] <- value

# S4 method for class 'SpatVoxel'
show(object)

Arguments

x

A SpatVoxel.

...

For c(): further rasters to combine with x, as with terra's c(). The result is a SpatVoxel with each layer's depth and the depth edges of every SpatVoxel among them, or a plain SpatRaster when the layers don't make a valid voxel (for example two layers at the same depth). For subset(): passed to terra's subset().

subset, negate, NSE

For subset(), which [[ and $ also call: the layers to keep, as with terra's subset(). The result is a SpatVoxel that keeps each layer's depth through later operations.

i, j, value

For [[<-: the layer to replace, by number or name, and its new values, as with terra. A replaced layer keeps its depth.

object

A SpatVoxel. show() prints the class, the depth levels, whether the voxel carries depth edges (see depth_bounds()) and the time, then terra's description of the grid.

Details

A voxel may have interior gaps — a cell can be NA at one depth and non-NA at the depths above and below it.

Each layer stands for a slab of water around its depth. A voxel can carry the top and bottom of each slab, for example a netCDF file's depth bounds, set with the depth_bounds argument of as_voxel() or envelope_to_voxel() and read with depth_bounds(). volume(), envelope_to_voxel(), voxel_to_envelope(), intersect_3d(), intersects_3d() and mask() use these edges when the voxel has them for every layer, and work the edges out from the depths with their bounds argument when it doesn't. Each slab must contain its depth and have a positive height, and slabs must not overlap; gaps between them are allowed.

terra operations that keep the SpatVoxel class ([[, crop(), mask(), arithmetic, c()) keep the edges; an operation that returns a plain SpatRaster (app(), writing to a file) drops them. Combining a voxel that has edges with one that doesn't, with c(), leaves some layers without edges, so bounds applies to the result.

The depths stay through selecting layers ([[, $, subset()), replacing a layer with [[<-, c(), arithmetic, ifel(), crop() and mask(). The SpatVoxel methods for subset(), [[<- and c() keep them where terra alone would reset them to 0. A few terra operations drop them, such as app(), which also returns a plain SpatRaster. The package's functions then stop with an error; set the depths again with as_voxel(x, depths = ...) or terra::depth(). A plain SpatRaster (for example after methods::as(v, "SpatRaster")) gets terra's own behaviour: after a layer subset, its next operation resets the depths.

Slots

depth_edges

A data frame with columns depth, lower and upper, in metres positive down: the slab each depth stands for, from lower (its top) to upper (its bottom), as in SpatProxy. It has no rows when the voxel carries no edges. Each layer finds its slab by its depth, so the table may hold rows for depths the voxel no longer has.

See also

SpatEnvelope, SpatVolume

Examples

# Two cells sampled at three standard depths. Build one with as_voxel(),
# which sets the depths and sorts the layers shallow to deep.
r <- terra::rast(nrows = 1, ncols = 2, xmin = 0, xmax = 2, ymin = 0,
                 ymax = 1, nlyrs = 3)
terra::values(r) <- cbind(c(12, 11), c(9, NA), c(6, 5))
v <- as_voxel(r, depths = c(0, 100, 200), varname = "temp")

depths(v)         # depth is stored per layer, in terra::depth()
#> [1]   0 100 200
terra::values(v)  # ...and the variable in the cell values
#>      temp_depth=0 temp_depth=100 temp_depth=200
#> [1,]           12              9              6
#> [2,]           11             NA              5

# Note cell 2: NA at 100 m, but with values above and below it. A voxel can
# hold that interior gap; a SpatEnvelope cannot.

# It is an ordinary SpatRaster underneath, so terra operations work on it
# unchanged. Re-wrapping with as_voxel() is cheap either way, since the
# constructor is idempotent.
methods::is(v, "SpatRaster")
#> [1] TRUE
terra::nlyr(terra::crop(v, terra::ext(0, 1, 0, 1)))
#> [1] 3
identical(depths(as_voxel(v)), depths(v))
#> [1] TRUE

# Layer names are labels: renaming keeps the depths.
names(v) <- c("surface", "mid", "deep")
depths(v)
#> [1]   0 100 200

# Selecting layers keeps their depths through later operations.
depths(terra::crop(v[[2:3]], terra::ext(0, 1, 0, 1)) * 2)
#> [1] 100 200

# The class checks run on construction: the depths must be set, distinct
# and run shallow to deep.
try(methods::new("SpatVoxel", r))
#> Error in validObject(.Object) : 
#>   invalid class “SpatVoxel” object: depths must be set in terra::depth(); set them with as_voxel(x, depths = ...) or terra::depth()
